what: DERIVATION, independent attempt 2 of 4: Two neutral inclusions in an ordered medium: the fluctuation attraction. SETTING (blocks 39, 40, 41; open PRs titled 'ail39: records that move', 'ail40', 'ail41: what a source is'): records move and carry their content; a site is empty or holds one record (content = one of the six axes); two neighbouring records weigh W = c * omega (omega = p, q, r for equal, opposite, orthogonal contents), a bond with an empty end weighs 1, a record weighs z; the neutral scale is c_0 = 6/(p+q+4r), at which every row of W sums to 6 and records do not bind on any window without a cycle (all binding is the loop factor 1 + 3 l_1^n + 2 l_2^n, l_1 = (p-q)/(p+q+4r), l_2 = (p+q-2r)/(p+q+4r)). Motion: a record hops to an empty neighbour, choosing between its two positions in proportion to the pair weights it would have there (an isolated record hops symmetrically). Formation: an empty site x forms a record at rate z Z_x, Z_x = sum over contents a of the product of W(a, s_y) over the recorded neighbours y, content drawn in proportion to the summand; records are never removed. BLOCK 41 PROVED: (1) the only local additive invariant density is the occupancy: mass = number of records; (2) two sets of records separated by empty sites weigh the product of their weights, at any scale: no action across empty sites; (3) the field of a held record through a medium is the pair correlation, of short range (ladder exact; cubic lattice about one step or less away from the clumping onset); (4) the content field around a record is a number times its content vector, zero for a record of unread content: the mass has no charge in the long-range tilt channel; (5) under symmetric hops with one record per site d<n_x>/dt = kappa * (lattice Laplacian of <n>)_x + j_x exactly, j the mean formation rate, so a steady excess of production carries the stationary halo G * (j - mean j)/kappa with G the lattice Green function (one-over-distance on Z^3); at the neutral scale the formation rate next to ONE record is exactly the void's (Z_x = 6), next to records of independent uniform contents it is the void's on average, and next to k agreeing records it is larger by 6^(k-1) (p^k+q^k+4r^k)/(p+q+4r)^k (13/12, 5/4 at (3,1,2); 46/21, 2348/343 at (12,1,2); k = 2, 3). NOT YET KNOWN: what a lump's halo looks like, how strong it is, and what a second lump does inside it. TASK: block 41's symmetry lemma says a record of unread content (a mass) has no LINEAR coupling to the tilt field of an ordered medium; it can couple only through rotation-invariant combinations. Work in the quadratic model (real field theta on the torus, weight exp(-(kappa/2) sum over bonds (theta_x - theta_y)^2), zero mode removed, covariance G/kappa). An inclusion at site x changes the stiffness of the six bonds at x from kappa to kappa(1 + epsilon) (epsilon = -1: a vacancy). (a) Derive the exact interaction free energy of two inclusions at x and y, F(x,y) = F_both - F_x - F_y + F_none, as (1/2) log det of a finite matrix built from second differences of G; (b) expand to second order in epsilon: F = -(epsilon^2/4) * sum over bond pairs of (second difference of G between the bonds)^2 + ..., show it is negative (attraction) for every epsilon sign combination that is equal, and find its decay on Z^3 (expected: one over r^6) with the exact constant from the continuum Green function; (c) compare with the one-over-r interaction of two held tilts (block 41, T4): ratio at r = 5, 10, 20 for epsilon = -1; (d) say whether any rotation-invariant inclusion can produce a one-over-r attraction, and prove the answer. check.py: exact F on the 8^3 torus with Fractions or high-precision rationals for epsilon = -1/2 at r = 1..4 against the second-order formula.  DELIVERABLE, in your unit worktree on ai/probes: probes/work/derive/source-neutral-inclusion-attraction/<your worker name>/ATTEMPT.md and check.py. ATTEMPT.md: (1) the exact statement you attempt; (2) numbered steps, each marked PROVED (argument given in full), CHECKED (a finite fact check.py verifies exactly) or ASSUMED; (3) if the route fails, the FIRST step that fails and why: a precise no-go for a route is a result; (4) what would finish it. check.py: exact arithmetic (fractions, integers, sympy) for every finite claim; it prints `SUMMARY: PROVED ...`, `SUMMARY: COUNTEREXAMPLE ...`, `SUMMARY: PARTIAL <what is new and exact>` or `SUMMARY: ROUTE FAILS AT <step>`, and a line `HIT: <the claim>` ONLY when you claim a proof, a counterexample, or a new exact partial result others can build on; a HIT is handed to a worker of another model family to referee line by line, so write for a hostile reader. Rules: definitions come from the notes on the PR branches named above (git fetch origin <branch>; git show origin/<branch>:<note>; find them with gh pr view <n> --json files,headRefName); any outside theorem you use must be re-proved at the scope you use it or listed under ASSUMED; no status words (proved theorems are promoted by the supervisor after the referee). Have your own plan BEFORE reading the prior attempts printed at claim time; then either build on a refereed partial result or take a different route. Run: python3 probes/run_probe.py <task> --worker <name> --model <model> --review "..." --extra "python3 probes/work/derive/source-neutral-inclusion-attraction/<name>/check.py"
